kurz: How the economy fluctuates irregularly around its growth path, and why the asymmetry of short recessions and long upswings argues against timing purchases and sales by the cycle.

bloecke.md:
The business cycle refers to the deviation of economic output from its long-term growth, not to the growth itself. An economy that has been growing steadily at 1.2% for years shows no cyclical fluctuations. If, on the other hand, growth swings back and forth between +3% and -2%, there is a cycle. What is measured is the utilisation of the existing stock of labour and capital.

The usual textbook chart shows a sine curve with four phases of equal length: recovery, boom, downturn and trough. In reality, the cycle is asymmetric. Upswings last for years and are gradual, downturns last for months and are steep. For investors, it is above all this skew that matters.

bloecke.erklaerung: The formula describes the expenditure approach of the national accounts. It breaks down economic output according to who ultimately buys it, and so shows which part fluctuates over the cycle.
variablen: gross investment: machinery and equipment, construction, intellectual property, changes in inventories
bloecke.beispiel: In Germany, roughly half of GDP is accounted for by private consumption and about a fifth each by government consumption and investment. Private consumption, the largest item, fluctuates much less than investment, which fluctuates the most of the three items.

bloecke.md:
Private consumption stabilises the cycle. Households smooth their spending, because rent, food and insurance still have to be paid even when income fluctuates. The fluctuations come mainly from investment. A company can postpone buying a machine by a year without suffering an immediate disadvantage. In a downturn, many companies do this at the same time. In addition, there is the inventory cycle. When demand falls, firms initially keep producing for stock, then cut production twice as sharply to run down inventories, and build them up twice as sharply when demand picks up. This is why new orders fluctuate many times more than GDP, even though they account for only a fraction of it.

Construction is the sector most sensitive to interest rates, because construction decisions lock in the interest burden for twenty years and a single percentage point can decide whether a project pays off. In August 2026, the German construction purchasing managers' index, at 48.7 points, was one of the few major sentiment indices below the growth threshold of 50. US housing starts fell to 1.275 million units, the lowest level since May 2026.

## Quarterly figures and reporting conventions

Two mistakes are easy to make when reading a GDP release. The first concerns the difference between nominal and real. Only real GDP measures volumes, and with inflation of just under 3%, an economy can grow significantly in nominal terms while stagnating in real terms. The second concerns the reporting convention. Germany and Eurostat report the change on the previous quarter, while the US reports it annualised, that is, extrapolated as if the quarterly pace continued for a whole year.

The reported figures were: US +1.5% (annualised, second estimate of 26 August 2026), euro area +0.6% on the previous quarter, Germany +0.2% on the previous quarter (flash estimate of 30 July 2026).

Converted to the quarterly pace, the US figure is 1.015^(1/4) − 1 = 0.0037, or around 0.37%.

Extrapolated to a full year, the euro area figure is 1.006^4 − 1 = 0.0242, or around 2.4%, and the German figure 1.002^4 − 1 = 0.008, or around 0.8%.

On an annualised basis, the ranking for the second quarter of 2026 is therefore: euro area around 2.4%, US 1.5%, Germany 0.8%. Simply comparing the reported figures of 1.5 and 0.6 reverses the order.

GDP figures go through a flash estimate, a second estimate, detailed results and, later, comprehensive revisions. For Germany's second quarter of 2026, the flash estimate gives +0.2%, while the detailed results of 25 August already give +0.3%. Destatis has thus revised the figure up by 0.1 percentage points. In the US, the annual benchmark revision of the labour market data has on several occasions retroactively removed several hundred thousand jobs. The third estimate of 30 September raised annualised US growth in the second quarter of 2026 from 1.5% to 2.2%. An investment decision that depends on the first decimal place of a first release is therefore based on a figure that still lies within the range of measurement error.

## Defining a recession

The rule of thumb used by the press says that two consecutive quarters of falling real GDP mean a recession. This rule is unambiguous, but it gives the wrong result as soon as a slightly positive quarter falls in between or a revision changes the sign.

In the US, a committee of the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) dates the turning points according to three criteria: the depth, duration and breadth of the decline across several series such as income, employment, production and consumption. This is why the slump from February to April 2020 counted as a recession, even though it lasted only two months. It was extremely deep and affected all areas at the same time. This thoroughness takes time, because the dating usually comes only with a delay of around a year. For the euro area, the committee of the Centre for Economic Policy Research performs this task; in Germany there is no official dating body.

bloecke.unter: The twelve recessions lasted between two and eighteen months, so at most a year and a half.

bloecke.titel: US cycles according to NBER dating

bloecke.md:
The eleven completed cycles give an average expansion length of around 67 months, with a median of 58 months and a range of 12 to 128 months. Since the extreme values differ by a factor of ten, the mean is not suitable for a forecast. More important than how long an upswing has lasted so far is the reason why it ends. The triggers are a tightening of monetary policy, a supply shock or the bursting of a credit-financed excess; age alone does not end an upswing. The statement “the upswing is already seven years old” therefore contains no information about the next year.

Taking recessions and expansions together, the US economy has spent around one seventh of the time in recession since 1949. An investor who wants to avoid the ten bad months risks missing part of the sixty good ones. Since the dating is only settled in hindsight, this risk is not merely theoretical.

## Timing of indicators

Indicators are classified by when they reflect the business cycle, not by how well they measure it. Investors who read a lagging indicator as if it were a forecast therefore regularly act too late. This error is systematic, not a matter of chance.

bloecke.md:
A diffusion index measures the breadth of a development. The value of 54.3 means that more manufacturing firms report increases than decreases. It does not show how large the increases are. In autumn 2026, this difference is clearly visible. The German manufacturing purchasing managers' index reached its highest level since May 2022 in August, while total industrial production in July was 1.8% below the previous year according to revised figures, and production excluding energy and construction just over 3% below. Good sentiment in surveys therefore does not yet mean higher sales.

The order statistics also need to be read with caution. German new orders rose by 2.5% in July according to the first release (3.2% after revision), the third month in a row. The increase was driven almost entirely by large orders in shipbuilding, rail vehicle construction and aircraft construction, which rose by 126.4%, while orders for motor vehicles fell by 12.5%. This is why the series is also published excluding large orders. If you look only at the headline, three ships can look like a turnaround.

The sector rotation model assigns winning sectors to each phase of the cycle. In the early recovery these are cyclicals, financials and real estate; in the boom, industrials, technology and energy; in the downturn, consumer staples, healthcare and utilities. The model describes past cycles reasonably well. As a guide to investment decisions it fails for three reasons: the phase is only settled in hindsight, the official dating comes with a delay of around a year, and the market prices in the expected rotation before it becomes visible in the economic data. In addition, the sample is small, around a dozen cycles since 1945, in which chance hits can look like fixed laws.

bloecke.titel: Four macro regimes by growth and inflation
bloecke.unter: For investment decisions, the combination of the directions of growth and inflation is more informative than the name of the cycle phase.

felder.text: Growth falls, prices rise. The central bank can only stabilise one of the two. This is where autumn 2026 stood.
Demand exceeds capacity, wages and prices pick up. This is usually followed by tightening and then the end of the upswing.
In a demand shock, growth and price pressure fall together. This is what rate cuts are designed for.
Spare capacity still available, productivity rising, price pressure remains low. Historically the most favourable combination for equities and bonds alike.

bloecke.md:
In practice, the distinction between a supply shock and a demand shock is the most important distinction in this topic. In a demand shock, growth and inflation move in the same direction, and monetary policy can respond unambiguously. In a supply shock, the two diverge, and every central bank decision that stabilises one of the two variables makes the other worse.

This is the situation the economy is in as of September 2026. Within a few days, the Brent price rose from $109.51 to $130.80 per barrel. German inflation rose from 2.3% in June to 2.9% in August, with the energy component up 10.5%. In the US, the headline rate was 3.4%, while the core rate was only 2.4%. Measured by the consumer price indices, the price pressure is therefore imported and not rooted in the domestic economy. Both central banks have nevertheless tightened monetary policy. The ECB raised the deposit facility rate to 2.50% with effect from 16 September 2026, and the Fed raised its target range to 3.75-4.00% with effect from 17 September 2026.

The classic recession signals show nothing here. On 18 September, at +0.25 percentage points (ten years versus two years) and +0.87 percentage points (ten years versus three months), the US yield curve had a normal shape, and the real-time value of the Sahm rule, at −0.07 points in August, was far below the trigger threshold of +0.50. An external disruption to the cycle does not show up in indicators that are calibrated to weak demand.

Section 1 of the Stability and Growth Act (StabG) commits the federal and state governments to macroeconomic equilibrium. This comprises price stability, a high level of employment and external equilibrium with steady and adequate growth, together known as the magic square. Section 2 StabG is the source of the Annual Economic Report, which the federal government presents at the beginning of each year. Under Section 6(1) SVRG (Council of Economic Experts Act), the German Council of Economic Experts (Sachverständigenrat) presents its annual report by 15 November. The German debate on the economic cycle therefore follows a calendar laid down by law.

The first place to apply knowledge of the cycle is your own income. For most households, the largest cyclical risk lies in earned income, not in the equity allocation of the portfolio. Under Section 105 SGB III (Social Code Book III, employment promotion), short-time work allowance (Kurzarbeitergeld) replaces 60% of the net pay difference, or 67% with a child, and under Section 104 SGB III it is paid for twelve months at most, or up to 24 months by regulation for entitlements arising by the end of 2026. Under Section 142 SGB III, unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld) requires twelve months of compulsory insurance within the reference period (Rahmenfrist). Under Section 147 SGB III, the duration of entitlement depends on age and the prior insurance period. Employees in cyclical industries need a larger emergency fund, measured in months of expenses and not as a percentage of the portfolio.

The second application is tax, because it follows the interest rate cycle. The advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) on accumulating funds under Section 18 InvStG (Investment Tax Act) depends on the base interest rate (Basiszins), which the Bundesbank derives at the start of each year from the yield on long-dated public bonds. For 2021 and 2022 it was not due, because the base interest rate was negative (−0.45% and −0.05%). Since the turn in the interest rate cycle, it has been payable again. Under Section 20(9) EStG (Income Tax Act), the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 (€2,000 for joint assessment) still covers it for smaller portfolios.

The cycle is not suitable as a signal for timing purchases and sales. A fixed rebalancing rule automatically buys more of whatever has fallen during downturns, without you having to identify the phase.

The cycle is useful for explaining, not as a timetable for investment decisions. It reliably shows why new orders turn earlier than the unemployment rate, but not reliably when. Any strategy that needs to know the phase in real time requires knowledge that even the NBER only provides a year later.

The specialist literature distinguishes fluctuations by length and cause: the inventory cycle of around three to five years (Kitchin), the investment cycle of about seven to eleven years (Juglar), the construction and infrastructure cycle of fifteen to twenty-five years (Kuznets) and the long waves of forty to sixty years (Kondratieff).

The first two are well supported empirically, because inventory holding and investment decisions can be observed directly. The long waves are disputed, because two hundred years of data contain only three to four complete cycles, which is not enough to separate patterns from chance. In any case, only the superposition of the cycles can be observed. A weak inventory cycle during a strong investment phase appears as a dip in monthly data and cannot be seen in annual data.

mitnehmen: The business cycle is the deviation from the growth path and is asymmetric; since 1948, US recessions have lasted 10.3 months on average, and the subsequent expansions around 67 months.
German and US GDP figures are only comparable after conversion, because 1.5% annualised corresponds to around 0.37% on the previous quarter.

Leading indicators run ahead of the business cycle, while lagging indicators such as the unemployment rate only turn after the turning point, so investors who wait for them act against a cycle that is already under way.

Whether growth and inflation move in the same or in opposite directions says more about the situation than any phase name, because in a supply shock the central bank can only stabilise one of the two variables.
Sector rotation describes past cycles well and predicts future ones poorly, because the phase is only settled in hindsight and the market anticipates it.

begriffe.text: Fluctuation of aggregate capacity utilisation around the long-term growth path, measured by production, income, employment and consumption. Phases and lengths are irregular, and the turning points are only settled in hindsight.

Quarterly change extrapolated to a full year, the usual form of reporting in the US. The conversion to the quarterly rate is (1 + annual rate)^(1/4) − 1. Germany and Eurostat, by contrast, report the change on the previous quarter directly.

Survey index that measures how many respondents report an improvement, not how large it is. The threshold of 50 separates growth from contraction. Purchasing managers' indices are the best-known example.

Disruption on the production side, such as a jump in energy prices, that drives inflation up and economic output down. Unlike in a demand shock, monetary policy cannot stabilise both variables at the same time.

Investment model that assigns typical winning sectors to each phase of the business cycle. It is plausible in hindsight but weak as a forecast, because the phase is unknown in real time and the market anticipates the rotation.
